name: Google Analytics for Firebase
notes: Collects an app-instance ID and the Android Advertising ID automatically (ad ID collection can be disabled in Analytics configuration; app-instance ID via the Consent Mode API). Google Signals, linking Google Ads, and Data Sharing Settings can change what is collected and whether it counts as shared; if you link Google Ads or export audiences, also declare PSL_ADVERTISING and review "shared".

data.what: Derived from the device's masked IP address
App lifecycle events: screen views and sessions

data.condition: Only if the app sells in-app products or subscriptions (purchase events are logged automatically)
Only if you call setUserId, or enable Google Signals (signed-in account identifiers)

name: Firebase Crashlytics
notes: Automatically sends stack traces, app state and device metadata at crash time, plus a Crashlytics installation UUID. Depends on Firebase Installations and Sessions. Custom keys, logs and user IDs you attach are also sent, so declare whatever they contain.

data.what: Application state and point-in-time device metadata at crash time
Crashlytics installation UUID (rotates with the Firebase installation ID)

data.condition: Only if you attach a user ID to crash reports (setUserId)

name: Firebase Authentication
notes: Always collects the device IP address (security and abuse prevention during sign-up and sign-in) and a generated Firebase Auth user ID. Other data depends on the sign-in methods you enable. Federated providers may also return profile/contact info depending on the scopes you request.

data.condition: Only with email/password, email link, or a federated provider that returns an email
Only with phone auth, phone as a sign-in method, or SMS second factor
Only if you set a display name or a federated provider returns one

name: Cloud Firestore
notes: Firestore stores whatever end-user data your app writes; declare those types yourself. The SDK itself sends only the Firebase user agent, plus the Firebase Auth user ID on every request when a user is signed in.

data.condition: Only if a user is signed in with Firebase Authentication

name: Firebase Cloud Messaging
notes: Sends app version and the Firebase user agent, and depends on Firebase Installations (installation ID and token). Purpose is message delivery; if you send marketing or product messages, also declare PSL_DEVELOPER_COMMUNICATIONS. Delivery metrics go to BigQuery only if you enable that export.

data.what: Via Firebase Installations (installation ID / FCM registration token)

name: Firebase Performance Monitoring
notes: Collects app start time, network request latency, CPU and memory usage, and device metadata. Also collects the IP address to map events to countries (decide whether to declare approximate location). Depends on Installations, Remote Config and Sessions. Custom traces, metrics and attributes you define are also sent.

name: Firebase Remote Config
notes: Sends country code, language code, time zone, OS/platform version, app ID and package name for parameter targeting, and depends on Firebase Installations. With Google Analytics included, user properties and first_open are used for targeting.

name: Firebase Installations
notes: Collects the Firebase installation ID (FID), a per-installation identifier that Google says does not uniquely identify a user or device, plus the Firebase user agent. Usually pulled in transitively by Messaging, Crashlytics, Performance and Remote Config. The page does not state a purpose.

name: Firebase AI Logic (formerly Vertex AI in Firebase)
notes: Sends whatever "developer-defined end-user data" your app puts in requests (prompts, images, files), so declare the matching types. Sends the Firebase Auth user ID on every request if a user is signed in. If AI monitoring is enabled in the console, prompts and outputs from sampled requests are retained.

data.condition: If the app sends user-written prompts or text
If the app sends user photos/images to the model
Only if a user is signed in with Firebase Authentication

name: Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob)
notes: All four types are collected and shared automatically for advertising, analytics and fraud prevention. Ad ID collection can be stopped via the manifest, and Limited Ads may stop ad ID transmission. The page covers play-services-ads only; ads-lite is assumed to behave the same. Optional features or tests may require extra disclosures.

data.what: IP address, which may be used to estimate general location
App launch time, hang rate, energy usage
Advertising ID, app set ID, and identifiers of signed-in accounts if applicable

name: Google User Messaging Platform (UMP) SDK
notes: No vendor Play disclosure for UMP was found; the AdMob page only links to it. UMP is normally used alongside the Google Mobile Ads SDK, whose disclosure covers the ads data. No data types are listed here; verify before relying on this.

name: RevenueCat Purchases SDK
notes: RevenueCat collects purchase history (not optional, not ephemeral) and acts as a service provider. Mark it shared too if you forward data to non-service-provider integrations. Locale and currency are collected but are not location. No crash logs or diagnostics.

data.condition: Only if you store it in customer attributes
Only if you store it in customer attributes
Only if you store it in customer attributes
Only if you use integrations that rely on advertising identifiers (GAID, Android ID)

name: Google Play Billing Library
notes: No vendor Play disclosure page for the Billing Library was found. Google's Data safety help says payment data collected directly by the payment service (and never accessed by your app) need not be declared, but purchase history your app or backend receives should be reviewed. Declare purchase history if you send purchase tokens or orders off-device.

data.condition: If the app or its backend stores or verifies purchases (tokens, order IDs) off-device

name: Sign in with Google / Credential Manager
notes: No vendor Play disclosure for these libraries was found (the Play services page covers only base, basement, oss-licenses and tasks). The sign-in flow returns the user's name, email and Google account ID to the app; declare them only if the app sends them (or the ID token) off-device, e.g. to its own backend.

data.condition: If the app sends the profile or ID token off-device
If the app sends the profile or ID token off-device
If the app sends the Google account ID or ID token off-device

name: ML Kit (on-device APIs)
notes: ML Kit sends only metadata (device and app info, identifiers, latency, API config, input/output size, event types, error codes) for diagnostics and usage analytics, and does not transfer it to third parties. The page does not list images, text or other feature inputs as collected. Thin features add a device identifier; GenAI features add user or device identifiers.

data.what: Per-installation identifiers always; a device identifier for thin (Play services) features

name: OneSignal Android SDK
notes: App interactions (sessions, notification clicks) are always collected. Other types depend on what you send: email/phone if added to OneSignal, personal data via Tags or Outcomes, precise location if your app collects and sends it, device IDs if you link identifiers with Aliases (no GAID by default). The vendor's purpose answers for the conditional types are shown only in screenshots and were not captured.

data.condition: If your app has in-app purchases
Only if your app collects location and sends it to OneSignal
Only if you add email subscriptions to OneSignal
Only if you add SMS subscriptions to OneSignal
Only if sent via Tags or Outcomes
Only if sent via Tags or Outcomes
Only if sent via Tags or Outcomes
Only if you link identifiers with Aliases

name: Facebook Android SDK (core, app events, login, share)
notes: Meta publishes no Play Data safety guidance (the Play SDK Index lists it as "Not provided"); this is inferred from Meta's automatic event logging docs. App events (install, launch, Google Play purchases) and app metadata are logged automatically unless AutoLogAppEventsEnabled is false; since v13 the SDK adds the AD_ID permission. Meta uses this data for its own ads products, so it is treated as shared.

data.what: Automatic app events (install, launch) unless AutoLogAppEventsEnabled=false

data.condition: Only if the app sells in-app products and automatic purchase logging is on (the default)

data.what: Advertising ID (AD_ID permission added since SDK 13.0.0)
Facebook SDK crash reports (SDK crashes only, for Meta's internal use)

data.condition: Only with Facebook Login, if the app sends the profile off-device
Only with Facebook Login and the email permission, if sent off-device
Only with Facebook Login, if the app sends the user ID or token off-device

name: Sentry Android SDK
notes: Sentry gives no per-type Play table; its mobile privacy FAQ names Analytics and App Functionality as standard purposes and says it uses a random per-installation ID, not ANDROID_ID. Types are inferred from its Data Collected page: device context, HTTP headers/bodies and IP (when userInfo is on) may be sent. Session Replay and breadcrumbs can add more; declare what you enable.

data.what: Device context always; performance data if tracing is enabled
Random installation ID when no user ID is set

data.condition: Only if you call Sentry.setUser() or an integration adds user identity

name: Mixpanel Android SDK
notes: No Mixpanel Play Data safety page was found; inferred from the Android SDK docs. The SDK assigns a device ID / distinct_id, sends the events you track (and autocapture clicks if enabled), and geolocates from the request IP unless UseIpAddressForGeolocation=false. optOutTracking() can stop collection; declare event properties you add yourself.

data.what: IP-based geolocation, unless UseIpAddressForGeolocation is false

data.condition: Only if you call identify() with your own user ID

name: OpenAI client libraries
notes: No vendor Play disclosure exists. The libraries send whatever the app puts in requests to the OpenAI API. Commonly treated as a service provider (not shared); decide based on your agreement with OpenAI. Calling the API straight from the app also ships your API key.

data.condition: If the app sends user-written prompts or text
If the app sends user images (vision input)
If the app sends voice recordings (transcription, realtime audio)
If the app uploads user files

name: Google AI client SDK for Android (Gemini API)
notes: No vendor Play disclosure exists for this SDK (Google recommends migrating to Firebase AI Logic, which has one). It sends whatever the app puts in requests to the Gemini API. Decide "shared" based on your Gemini API terms.

data.condition: If the app sends user-written prompts or text
If the app sends user images
